description: A complex structure in a multi-phase cemetery which produced both prehistoric and early medieval funerary material. In the Roman phase we see a circular metalled bank, within which a square stone structure was built, the lining of which was directly over a Bronze Age barrow. This structure was also partly built over pit, which was cut quite regularly and associated with decorative bronze material, the pit also had a central socket at its base suggesting a pole was stood inside it. The square structure over the pit also showed decorative bronze material in its foundation level. The structure's unusual history, lack of domestic material, and location in a pre-historic cemetery has led to the suggestion that it should be considered a shrine.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Capel Eithin, Gaerwen (Gwynedd).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
White, and Smith. “A Funerary and Ceremonial Centre at Capel Eithin, Gaerwen, Anglesey.” Transactions of the Anglesey Antiquarian Society, 1999.
